title_en: The Science of the Talismanic Grids (ʿilm al-jadwal)
body_ar: لي والد يستعمل الجداول فما ذا أفعل معه؟ علم الجدول أو علم التربيع هو علم من علوم الشر يحرم تعلمه و تعليمه و الاشتغال به فكل ذلك حرام و إذا كان الإنسان معروفا باستعماله فهذا جرحة في شهادته لا تقبل شهادته في المسلمين فلذلك يجب نصيحته يجب على الإنسان أن ينصح والده بالتي هي أحسن (و إذا استطاع أن يسرق ما معه من الجداول فيتلفها بحيث لا يغضب عليه فذلك أفضل له يسرقها من كتبه أو من صندوقه و يتلفها بحيث لا يعلم بذلك الوالد.)
body_en:
I have a father who uses the grids (al-jadāwil). What am I to do about him?

The science of the grid, or the science of squaring (al-tarbīʿ), is one of the sciences of evil. Learning it, teaching it and occupying oneself with it are forbidden: all of that is forbidden (ḥarām). And if a person is known for using it, that is an impugnment of his standing as a witness (jurḥah): his testimony is not accepted among the Muslims. For that reason it is obligatory to counsel him — a person is obliged to counsel his father in the best manner. (And if he is able to steal the grids his father has and destroy them in such a way that his father does not become angry with him, that is better for him: he steals them from his books or from his chest and destroys them in such a way that the father does not come to know of it.)

flags.context: لي والد يستعمل الجداول … علم الجدول أو علم التربيع هو علم من علوم الشر
options: talismanic grids / the science of the grid, or of squaring (al-jadwal, al-tarbīʿ)
magic squares / the science of magic squares
letter-and-number squares used for talismans and divination
flags.note: al-jadāwil is on the style guide's list of glossary terms pending a fixed rendering (§13), and this article is the term's primary occurrence in the corpus. In the Mauritanian and wider West African context it denotes talismanic squares built from letters and numerals, used for protection and for divination; al-tarbīʿ ('squaring') is given here as a synonym. 'Magic squares' is the nearest English handle but carries the wrong, purely mathematical sense for many readers. The Sheikh's office should fix the rendering before this is published, and the same rendering should then be applied corpus-wide.

flags.arabic: و إذا استطاع أن يسرق ما معه من الجداول فيتلفها
options: steal (rendered literally, as the Arabic has it)
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW. The Arabic verb is saraqa, 'to steal', and it has been rendered literally rather than softened, per the house rule against softening. Read in English and out of context this is counsel to take and destroy a parent's property covertly, which carries obvious reputational and, in some jurisdictions, legal risk. The decision on whether and how to publish this passage belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office. Note also that the Sheikh's own stated obligation is to counsel the father 'in the best manner'; the destruction counsel is offered as a further step that is 'better for him', not as an obligation.

flags.arabic: (و إذا استطاع أن يسرق … لا يعلم بذلك الوالد.)
flags.context: the final sentence of the record, which is enclosed in round brackets in the source
options: treat the brackets as the site's own and reproduce them
treat the bracketed sentence as an editorial insertion and mark it as such
flags.note: The round brackets are in the source and their status is unclear: they may mark an aside in the spoken original, or an editorial addition by whoever prepared the text. They have been reproduced in both body_ar and body_en without interpretation. Worth resolving with the Sheikh's office, since the bracketed sentence is the passage flagged for editorial review above.

flags.context: و إذا كان الإنسان معروفا باستعماله فهذا جرحة في شهادته لا تقبل شهادته في المسلمين
options: an impugnment of his standing as a witness (jurḥah)
flags.note: jarḥ/jurḥah is the technical term of al-jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl, the appraisal of witnesses and narrators. The Sheikh is making a statement about admissibility of testimony in a court, not a general moral judgement, and the English should not be allowed to slide into the latter.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-21 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.

The questioner's question and the Sheikh's answer run together in a single unbroken paragraph in the source; a paragraph break has been introduced in body_en between them for readability, and body_ar is left as the source has it.
'It is obligatory to counsel him' renders yajibu naṣīḥatuhu; wājib is used by the Sheikh here in its ordinary legal sense.
The Sheikh gives no evidence or citation for the ruling in this record, and none has been supplied.
